title: MicroSim Suitability Judge
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AI for EE Research
description: Judgment activity in which learners decide, for eight illustrative pieces of electrical engineering research content, whether an interactive MicroSim or a static figure or text is the better medium. The criterion stays on screen; each item has one attempt in a fixed order, with Correct or The better medium is feedback and a one-sentence reason, and the activity ends with a score out of 8 and a mastery statement at 7 of 8.

educational.topic: Choosing between an interactive simulation and a static figure or text for research communication
learningObjectives: Judge, for each of eight pieces of research content, whether an interactive MicroSim or a static figure or text is the better medium, with at least 7 of 8 correct
prerequisites: Interactive simulation and MicroSim, as defined in the sections Communicating Research and MicroSims of Chapter 16
The criterion that a MicroSim suits a dependence or process the learner can manipulate or predict

accessibility.notes: describe() provides a screen-reader description; all controls are native HTML buttons reachable with the Tab key and activated with Enter or Space; the selected choice is marked with aria-pressed, bold text and an outline; correct and incorrect feedback uses words and check or X symbols as well as a color-blind-safe blue and vermillion; all body text is 16 px or larger.

controls.label: MicroSim
controls.purpose: Chooses MicroSim as the better medium for the current item. The choice can be changed until it is submitted; disabled after submission.

controls.label: Static figure or text
controls.purpose: Chooses static figure or text as the better medium for the current item. The choice can be changed until it is submitted; disabled after submission.

controls.label: Submit / Next Item / See Score
controls.purpose: Submit commits the single attempt for the current item and shows the feedback; Next Item advances to the next item in the fixed order; See Score, after item 8, shows n of 8 correct and whether the mastery threshold of 7 was met.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Criterion-based binary judgment with one attempt per item and immediate explanatory feedback
keyQuestions: Would a learner understand this better by changing something?
Does the content have a parameter the learner can change?
Is there a process the learner can step through or predict?
commonMisconceptions: Interactive is always better than static
Any technical content should become a simulation
A table of values is equivalent to a sim of the function
assessmentOpportunities: At least 7 of 8 judgments matching the answer key on the first attempt is evidence of mastery
Reading the criterion is exploration and is not evidence
